From 5efe9688f9488e8e95177d03be2678021233e877 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Steven Rostedt (Google)" <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2024 15:25:50 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] ftrace/selftests: Fix pid test with function graph not
 showing pids

The pid filtering test will set the pid filters and make sure that both
function and function_graph tracing honors the filters. But the
function_graph tracer test was failing because the PID was not being
filtered properly. That's because the funcgraph-proc option wasn't getting
set. Without that option the PID is not shown.

Instead we get:

	+ cat trace
	# tracer: function_graph
	#
	# CPU  DURATION                  FUNCTION CALLS
	# |     |   |                     |   |   |   |
	 3) ! 143.685 us  |  kernel_clone();
	 3) ! 127.055 us  |  kernel_clone();
	 1) ! 127.170 us  |  kernel_clone();
	 3) ! 126.840 us  |  kernel_clone();

When we should be getting:

	+ cat trace
	# tracer: function_graph
	#
	# CPU  TASK/PID         DURATION                  FUNCTION CALLS
	# |     |    |           |   |                     |   |   |   |
	 4)    bash-939    | # 1070.009 us |  kernel_clone();
	 4)    bash-939    | # 1116.903 us |  kernel_clone();
	 5)    bash-939    | ! 976.133 us  |  kernel_clone();
	 5)    bash-939    | ! 954.012 us  |  kernel_clone();

The test looks for the pids it is filtering and will fail if it can not
find them. Without fungraph-proc option set, it will not be displayed and
the test will fail.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/Zl9JFnzKGuUM10X2@J2N7QTR9R3/
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-trace-kernel/20240604152550.0c01d7cd@gandalf.local.home

Cc: Masami Hiramatsu <mhiramat@kernel.org>
Cc: Mathieu Desnoyers <mathieu.desnoyers@efficios.com>
Fixes: 35b944a997e2 ("selftests/ftrace: Add function_graph tracer to func-filter-pid test")
Reported-by: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (Google) <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Tested-by: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/ftrace/test.d/ftrace/func-filter-pid.tc b/tools/testing/selftests/ftrace/test.d/ftrace/func-filter-pid.tc
index c6fc9d31a496..8dcce001881d 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/ftrace/test.d/ftrace/func-filter-pid.tc
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/ftrace/test.d/ftrace/func-filter-pid.tc
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 # Also test it on an instance directory
 
 do_function_fork=1
+do_funcgraph_proc=1
 
 if [ ! -f options/function-fork ]; then
     do_function_fork=0
@@ -28,6 +29,7 @@ fi
 
 if [ $do_funcgraph_proc -eq 1 ]; then
     orig_value2=`cat options/funcgraph-proc`
+    echo 1 > options/funcgraph-proc
 fi
 
 do_reset() {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/testing/selftests/ftrace/test.d/ftrace/func-filter-pid.tc`**
   - A new variable `do_funcgraph_proc` is introduced and set to `1`.
   - The script checks if `do_funcgraph_proc` is equal to `1`, and if so, it reads the current value of `options/funcgraph-proc` into `orig_value2`.
   - The script then sets `options/funcgraph-proc` to `1` to ensure that the function graph tracer displays the PID information.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications made in the `func-filter-pid.tc` file are directly related to fixing the issue where the function graph tracer was not displaying PIDs correctly during the PID filtering test. By setting the `funcgraph-proc` option to `1`, the patch ensures that the PID information is included in the output of the function graph tracer, which is essential for the test to pass. This change addresses the root cause of the test failure, as previously the absence of this option resulted in the PID not being shown, leading to incorrect test results.

The bug was caused by the `funcgraph-proc` option not being set, which resulted in the function graph tracer not displaying the PID information. This omission led to the PID filtering test failing, as the expected output included PIDs that were not shown without this option being enabled.
